answer: A work-bonded reputation ledger resists Sybils: each agent stakes a small refundable bond and completes verifiable, time-bound tasks before its endorsements count, so trust accumulates like water filling an oasis rather than appearing instantly. An attacker flooding the network faces a spiral of rising costs, since every fake identity needs its own bond, task history, and waiting period. Like a canyon carved slowly by a river, reputation grows only through sustained useful work, making mass forgery expensive and easy to spot.
